beats.text: Most people will tell you this is a wedding portrait of a pregnant bride.
beats.visuals: Empty-room plate (figures removed by layer) on near-black gallery matte; figures slide in from both sides at larger scale (HI-02 figure reveal / CAM-02 relative motion)
beats.highlight_sync: Most (room visible), pregnant -> figures finish arriving ~ end of beat
beats.sync_method: each beat = separate Chatterbox call; visual events start at beat start (exact)

beats.text: Look closer, because it is probably neither.
beats.visuals: Slow decelerating pull-back (0.33x over ~14s, ease-out) to the full vertical painting on matte
beats.highlight_sync: Look -> pull-back starts at beat start
beats.sync_method: each beat = separate Chatterbox call; visual events start at beat start (exact)

beats.text: Her green gown, held up in bunches, was a stock fertility pose, not a sign of pregnancy.
beats.visuals: Matte full painting zooms in until it fills width (ease-in), then continues push into dress; label GREEN GOWN / Jan van Eyck, 1434
beats.highlight_sync: Her -> push-in start; label pops ~0.6 s in
beats.sync_method: each beat = separate Chatterbox call; visual events start at beat start (exact)

beats.text: The fur lining is a boast, a billboard for Bruges luxury and Arnolfini wealth.

beats.sync_method: each beat = separate Chatterbox call; visual events start at beat start (exact)

beats.text: The little dog is a quiet echo of the pets carved beside women on medieval tombs.

beats.text: But the clue that matters most is in the hands.

beats.text: It reads less like a wedding record, and more like a memorial to a love that outlasts death.
